cases.name: restart_from_zero
cases.note: A transfer may be dropped and started again at seq 0.

cases.name: wrong_hash
cases.note: All bytes arrive but they do not hash to the announced value.

cases.name: not_json
cases.note: The bytes hash correctly but are not a device layout.

cases.name: no_memory
cases.note: The platform cannot give a block for the bytes.

cases.name: new_transfer_during_build
cases.note: seq 0 never answers busy. It drops the build that is still running; the old layout stays on screen. The second transfer then commits normally.

cases.name: header_too_big_first
cases.note: seq 0 checks too_big before the other header fields.

cases.name: header_checked_before_memory
cases.note: size is checked before anything is allocated.

cases.name: bad_header_drops_the_build
cases.note: A seq 0 call drops the unfinished transfer and any build in progress first, also when its header is refused. Nothing is left to commit.

cases.name: repeated_commit_while_building
cases.note: HA lost the answer to tab_commit and commits the same hash again: success, and the build carries on unchanged.

cases.name: repeated_commit_after_failed_build
cases.note: The build ran out of memory ('build_fails'), so the staged layout is gone: a repeated commit answers incomplete, and tab_status reports build 'memory'.

note: Each case starts on a fresh tablet that is not paired, so the auth argument of tab_commit is empty. 'expect' lists the result of each tab_layout call; 'commit' is the result of tab_commit(commit_hash or the first call's hash). 'platform.alloc_fails': no PSRAM block can be had. 'platform.build_fails': the build that follows the commit ends with that code. 'after_commit' holds calls made right after that commit (after the failed build with build_fails), 'building' whether a build runs after those calls, then tab_commit(commit_hash or their first hash). 'shown' is the hash on screen at the end (default: the hash when 'commit' is ok, else empty).
